The clue Glaze is a clear indicator of pottery, as it's a common technique used in the craft.
The clue Clay is a primary material used in pottery, which further supported my theory.
The clue Kiln was the turning point, as it's a specific type of oven used in pottery.
In hindsight, the clues were more obvious than I initially thought, but the multiple meanings made it tricky.
The key takeaway is to pay attention to the specific context of each clue to avoid misinterpretation.
By doing so, you can increase your chances of arriving at the correct answer.
solutionNarrative: Wheel and Ribs first pulled me toward woodworking tools, so that was the first path I tested. It held together for a moment, but kiln never really fit it. The more I pushed that first read, the more the board sounded stitched together instead of naturally solved.

The solve turned when I stopped treating kiln as just another clue and asked what kind of thing each clue could really be describing. I was no longer trying to rescue woodworking tools; I was checking whether Wheel and Ribs could survive the same tighter read.

Then I used Glaze, Clay, and Kiln as the confirmation round. Glaze, Clay, and Kiln stayed inside the real category, so the answer felt earned instead of guessed. The answer was Things used when making pottery.
